content.latin: ℣. Dómine, lábia + mea apéries.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

segments.t: Dómine, lábia + mea apéries.

content.latin: ℟. Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

segments.t: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius
(genuflectitur)
veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Apostles, * O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Ætérna Christi múnera,
content.english: Th' eternal gifts of Christ the King,

content.latin: Apostolórum glóriam,
content.english: The Apostles' glory, let us sing;

content.latin: Palmas et hymnos débitos
content.english: And all with hearts of gladness raise

content.latin: Lætis canámus méntibus.
content.english: Due hymns of thankful love and praise.

content.latin: Ecclesiárum Príncipes,
content.english: For they the Church's princes are,

content.latin: Belli triumpháles duces,
content.english: Triumphant leaders in the war,

content.latin: Cæléstis aulæ mílites,
content.english: The heavenly King's own warrior band,

content.latin: Et vera mundi lúmina.
content.english: True lights to lighten every land.

content.latin: Devóta Sanctórum fides,
content.english: Theirs was the steadfast faith of saints,

content.latin: Invícta spes credéntium,
content.english: The hope that never yields nor faints,

content.latin: Perfécta Christi cáritas
content.english: The love of Christ in perfect glow,

content.latin: Mundi tyránnum cónterit.
content.english: That lay the prince of this world low.

content.latin: In his Patérna glória,
content.english: In them the Father's glory shone,

content.latin: In his triúmphat Fílius,
content.english: In them the Spirit's will was done,

content.latin: In his volúntas Spíritus,
content.english: The Son himself exults in them;

content.latin: Cælum replétur gáudio.
content.english: Joy fills the new Jerusalem.

content.latin: Patri, simúlque Fílio,
content.english: Praise to the Father, with the Son,

content.latin: Tibíque Sancte Spíritus,
content.english: And Holy Spirit, Three in One;

content.latin: Sicut fuit, sit iúgiter
content.english: As ever was in ages past,

content.latin: Sæclum per omne glória.
content.english: And so shall be while ages last.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Nocturn I

content.english: Ant. The Lord saw Peter and Andrew, * and He called them.

Vidit Dóminus * Petrum et Andréam, et vocávit eos.

content.latin: Psalmus 18 [1]
content.english: Psalm 18 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 18

content.latin: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.
content.english: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

segments.t: Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.

content.latin: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
content.english: 18:3 Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.

segments.t: Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.

content.latin: 18:4 Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
content.english: 18:4 There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.

segments.t: Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.

content.latin: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: 18:5 Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: 18:6 In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
content.english: 18:6 He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,

segments.t: In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:

content.latin: 18:6 Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:
content.english: 18:6 Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * his going out is from the end of heaven,

segments.t: Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:

content.latin: 18:7 Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.
content.english: 18:7 And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.

segments.t: Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.

content.latin: 18:8 Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
content.english: 18:8 The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.

segments.t: Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.

content.latin: 18:9 Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
content.english: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

segments.t: Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.

content.latin: 18:10 Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.
content.english: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

segments.t: Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.

content.latin: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
content.english: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

segments.t: Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.

content.latin: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
content.english: 18:12 For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.

segments.t: Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.

content.latin: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
content.english: 18:13 Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.

segments.t: Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.

content.latin: 18:14 Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
content.english: 18:14 If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.

segments.t: Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.

content.latin: 18:15 Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
content.english: 18:15 And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.

segments.t: Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.

content.latin: 18:15 Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
content.english: 18:15 O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.

segments.t: Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Vidit Dóminus Petrum et Andréam, et vocávit eos.
content.english: Ant. The Lord saw Peter and Andrew, and He called them.

segments.t: Ant.
Vidit Dóminus Petrum et Andréam, et vocávit eos.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte post me, * dicit Dóminus, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.
content.english: Ant. Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men, * saith the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte post me, * dicit Dóminus, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.

content.latin: Psalmus 33 [2]
content.english: Psalm 33 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 33

content.latin: 33:2 Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.
content.english: 33:2 I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.

segments.t: Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.

content.latin: 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
content.english: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

segments.t: In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.

content.latin: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.
content.english: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

segments.t: Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.

content.latin: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
content.english: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

segments.t: Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.

content.latin: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
content.english: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

segments.t: Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.

content.latin: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.
content.english: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

segments.t: Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.

content.latin: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
content.english: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

segments.t: Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.

content.latin: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
content.english: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

segments.t: Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.

content.latin: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
content.english: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

segments.t: Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.

content.latin: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
content.english: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

segments.t: Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.

content.latin: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
content.english: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

segments.t: Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.

content.latin: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
content.english: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

segments.t: Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?

content.latin: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
content.english: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

segments.t: Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.

content.latin: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
content.english: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

segments.t: Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.

content.latin: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.
content.english: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

segments.t: Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.

content.latin: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
content.english: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

segments.t: Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.

content.latin: 33:18 Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

segments.t: Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.

content.latin: 33:19 Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
content.english: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

segments.t: Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.

content.latin: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
content.english: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

segments.t: Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.

content.latin: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
content.english: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

segments.t: Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.

content.latin: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.
content.english: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

segments.t: Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.

content.latin: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
content.english: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

segments.t: Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte post me, dicit Dóminus, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.
content.english: Ant. Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men, saith the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte post me, dicit Dóminus, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.

content.latin: Ant. Relíctis rétibus suis, * secúti sunt Dóminum Redemptórem.
content.english: Ant. And they left their nets, * and followed the Lord their Saviour.

segments.t: Ant.
Relíctis rétibus suis, * secúti sunt Dóminum Redemptórem.

content.latin: Psalmus 44 [3]
content.english: Psalm 44 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

segments.t: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

segments.t: Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

segments.t: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

segments.t: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

segments.t: Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

segments.t: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

segments.t: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

segments.t: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Relíctis rétibus suis, secúti sunt Dóminum Redemptórem.
content.english: Ant. And they left their nets, and followed the Lord their Saviour.

segments.t: Ant.
Relíctis rétibus suis, secúti sunt Dóminum Redemptórem.

content.latin: ℣. In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.
content.english: ℣. Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth:

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: ℟. And their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: De Epístola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Romános
content.english: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

content.latin: 4 Finis legis, Christus, ad iustítiam omni credénti.
content.english: 4 For the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to every one that believeth.

segments.t: Finis legis, Christus, ad iustítiam omni credénti.

content.latin: 5 Móyses enim scripsit, quóniam iustítiam, quæ ex lege est, qui fécerit homo, vivet in ea.
content.english: 5 For Moses wrote, that the justice which is of the law, the man that shall do it, shall live by it.

segments.t: Móyses enim scripsit, quóniam iustítiam, quæ ex lege est, qui fécerit homo, vivet in ea.

content.latin: 6 Quæ autem ex fide est iustítia, sic dicit: Ne díxeris in corde tuo: Quis ascéndet in cælum? id est, Christum dedúcere:
content.english: 6 But the justice which is of faith, speaketh thus: Say not in thy heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? that is, to bring Christ down;

segments.t: Quæ autem ex fide est iustítia, sic dicit: Ne díxeris in corde tuo: Quis ascéndet in cælum? id est, Christum dedúcere:

content.latin: 7 Aut, Quis descéndet in abýssum? hoc est, Christum a mórtuis revocáre.
content.english: 7 Or who shall descend into the deep? that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.

segments.t: Aut, Quis descéndet in abýssum? hoc est, Christum a mórtuis revocáre.

content.latin: 8 Sed quid dicit Scriptúra? Prope est verbum in ore tuo, et in corde tuo: hoc est verbum fídei, quod prædicámus.
content.english: 8 But what saith the scripture? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart. This is the word of faith, which we preach.

segments.t: Sed quid dicit Scriptúra? Prope est verbum in ore tuo, et in corde tuo: hoc est verbum fídei, quod prædicámus.

content.latin: 9 Quia si confiteáris in ore tuo Dóminum Iesum, et in corde tuo credíderis quod Deus illum suscitávit a mórtuis, salvus eris.
content.english: 9 For if thou confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in thy heart that God hath raised him up from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

segments.t: Quia si confiteáris in ore tuo Dóminum Iesum, et in corde tuo credíderis quod Deus illum suscitávit a mórtuis, salvus eris.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Cum perambuláret Dóminus iuxta mare Galilǽæ, vidit Petrum et Andréam rétia mitténtes in mare, et vocávit eos, dicens:
content.english: ℟. The Lord, walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw Peter and Andrew casting their nets into the sea, and He called them saying:

segments.t: Cum perambuláret Dóminus iuxta mare Galilǽæ, vidit Petrum et Andréam rétia mitténtes in mare, et vocávit eos, dicens:

content.latin: * Veníte post me, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.
content.english: * Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.

content.latin: ℣. Erant enim piscatóres, et ait illis.
content.english: ℣. For they were fishers, and He saith unto them:

segments.t: Erant enim piscatóres, et ait illis.

content.latin: ℟. Veníte post me, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.
content.english: ℟. Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.

segments.t: Veníte post me, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 10 Corde enim créditur ad iustítiam: ore autem conféssio fit ad salútem.
content.english: 10 For, with the heart, we believe unto justice; but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation.

segments.t: Corde enim créditur ad iustítiam: ore autem conféssio fit ad salútem.

content.latin: 11 Dicit enim Scriptúra: Omnis qui credit in illum, non confundétur.
content.english: 11 For the scripture saith: Whosoever believeth in him, shall not be confounded.

segments.t: Dicit enim Scriptúra: Omnis qui credit in illum, non confundétur.

content.latin: 12 Non enim est distínctio Iudǽi et Græci: nam idem Dóminus ómnium, dives in omnes qui ínvocant illum.
content.english: 12 For there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek: for the same is Lord over all, rich unto all that call upon him.

segments.t: Non enim est distínctio Iudǽi et Græci: nam idem Dóminus ómnium, dives in omnes qui ínvocant illum.

content.latin: 13 Omnis enim quicúmque invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit.
content.english: 13 For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved.

segments.t: Omnis enim quicúmque invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit.

content.latin: 14 Quómodo ergo invocábunt, in quem non credidérunt? aut quómodo credent ei, quem non audiérunt? quómodo autem áudient sine prædicánte?
content.english: 14 How then shall they call on him, in whom they have not believed? Or how shall they believe him, of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear, without a preacher?

segments.t: Quómodo ergo invocábunt, in quem non credidérunt? aut quómodo credent ei, quem non audiérunt? quómodo autem áudient sine prædicánte?

content.latin: 15 Quómodo vero prædicábunt nisi mittántur? sicut scriptum est: Quam speciósi pedes evangelizántium pacem, evangelizántium bona!
content.english: 15 And how shall they preach unless they be sent, as it is written: How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, of them that bring glad tidings of good things!

segments.t: Quómodo vero prædicábunt nisi mittántur? sicut scriptum est: Quam speciósi pedes evangelizántium pacem, evangelizántium bona!

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Mox ut vocem Dómini prædicántis audívit beátus Andréas, relíctis rétibus, quorum usu actúque vivébat,
content.english: ℟. As soon as the blessed Andrew heard the voice of the Lord calling him, he left his nets, by the exercise and use whereof he lived;

segments.t: Mox ut vocem Dómini prædicántis audívit beátus Andréas, relíctis rétibus, quorum usu actúque vivébat,

content.latin: * Ætérnæ vitæ secútus est prǽmia largiéntem.
content.english: * And followed Him Who giveth life everlasting.

content.latin: ℣. Hic est qui pro amóre Christi pepéndit in cruce, et pro lege eius sustínuit passiónem.
content.english: ℣. This is that disciple who for the love of Christ hung upon the cross, and suffered for the law of his God.

segments.t: Hic est qui pro amóre Christi pepéndit in cruce, et pro lege eius sustínuit passiónem.

content.latin: ℟. Ætérnæ vitæ secútus est prǽmia largiéntem.
content.english: ℟. And followed Him Who giveth life everlasting.

segments.t: Ætérnæ vitæ secútus est prǽmia largiéntem.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 16 Sed non omnes obédiunt Evangélio. Isaías enim dicit: Dómine, quis crédidit audítui nostro?
content.english: 16 But all do not obey the gospel. For Isaias saith: Lord, who hath believed our report?

segments.t: Sed non omnes obédiunt Evangélio. Isaías enim dicit: Dómine, quis crédidit audítui nostro?

content.latin: 17 Ergo fides ex audítu, audítus autem per verbum Christi.
content.english: 17 Faith then cometh by hearing; and hearing by the word of Christ.

segments.t: Ergo fides ex audítu, audítus autem per verbum Christi.

content.latin: 18 Sed dico: Numquid non audiérunt? Et quidem in omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: 18 But I say: Have they not heard? Yes, verily, their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the whole world.

segments.t: Sed dico: Numquid non audiérunt? Et quidem in omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: 19 Sed dico: Numquid Israël non cognóvit? Primus Móyses dicit: Ego ad æmulatiónem vos addúcam in non gentem: in gentem insipiéntem, in iram vos mittam.
content.english: 19 But I say: Hath not Israel known? First, Moses saith: I will provoke you to jealousy by that which is not a nation; by a foolish nation I will anger you.

segments.t: Sed dico: Numquid Israël non cognóvit? Primus Móyses dicit: Ego ad æmulatiónem vos addúcam in non gentem: in gentem insipiéntem, in iram vos mittam.

content.latin: 20 Isaías autem audet, et dicit: Invéntus sum a non quæréntibus me: palam appárui iis, qui me non interrogábant.
content.english: 20 But Isaias is bold, and saith: I was found by them that did not seek me: I appeared openly to them that asked not after me.

segments.t: Isaías autem audet, et dicit: Invéntus sum a non quæréntibus me: palam appárui iis, qui me non interrogábant.

content.latin: 21 Ad Israël autem dicit: Tota die expándi manus meas ad pópulum non credéntem, et contradicéntem.
content.english: 21 But to Israel he saith: All the day long have I spread my hands to a people that believeth not, and contradicteth me.

segments.t: Ad Israël autem dicit: Tota die expándi manus meas ad pópulum non credéntem, et contradicéntem.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Doctor bonus et amícus Dei Andréas dúcitur ad crucem, quam a longe aspíciens dixit: Salve, crux,
content.english: ℟. Andrew the good teacher, the friend of God, was led to the cross, and when he saw it afar off, he said: God bless thee, O cross;

segments.t: Doctor bonus et amícus Dei Andréas dúcitur ad crucem, quam a longe aspíciens dixit: Salve, crux,

content.latin: * Súscipe discípulum eius, qui pepéndit in te magíster meus Christus.
content.english: * Welcome to the follower of Him That hung on thee, even my Master Christ.

content.latin: ℣. Salve, crux, quæ in córpore Christi dedicáta es, et ex membris eius tamquam margarítis ornáta.
content.english: ℣. God bless thee, O cross, thou art hallowed by the Body of Christ; His Members make thee goodly as with pearls.

segments.t: Salve, crux, quæ in córpore Christi dedicáta es, et ex membris eius tamquam margarítis ornáta.

content.latin: ℟. Súscipe discípulum eius, qui pepéndit in te magíster meus Christus.
content.english: ℟. Be welcome to the follower of Him That hung on thee, even my Master Christ.

segments.t: Súscipe discípulum eius, qui pepéndit in te magíster meus Christus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Súscipe discípulum eius, qui pepéndit in te magíster meus Christus.
content.english: ℟. Be welcome to the follower of Him That hung on thee, even my Master Christ.

segments.t: Súscipe discípulum eius, qui pepéndit in te magíster meus Christus.

content.latin: Nocturnus II
content.english: Nocturn II

segments.t: Nocturnus II

content.latin: Ant. Dignum sibi Dóminus * computávit Mártyrem, quem vocávit Apóstolum, dum esset in mari, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Whom the Lord called to be His Apostle, * when he was by the sea, him also He counted worthy to be His martyr. Alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Dignum sibi Dóminus * computávit Mártyrem, quem vocávit Apóstolum, dum esset in mari, allelúia.

content.latin: Psalmus 46 [4]
content.english: Psalm 46 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 46

content.latin: 46:2 Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * iubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.
content.english: 46:2 O clap your hands, all ye nations: * shout unto God with the voice of joy,

segments.t: Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * iubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.

content.latin: 46:3 Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.
content.english: 46:3 For the Lord is high, terrible: * a great king over all the earth.

segments.t: Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.

content.latin: 46:4 Subiécit pópulos nobis: * et gentes sub pédibus nostris.
content.english: 46:4 He hath subdued the people under us; * and the nations under our feet.

segments.t: Subiécit pópulos nobis: * et gentes sub pédibus nostris.

content.latin: 46:5 Elégit nobis hereditátem suam: * spéciem Iacob, quam diléxit.
content.english: 46:5 He hath chosen for us his inheritance, * the beauty of Jacob which he hath loved.

segments.t: Elégit nobis hereditátem suam: * spéciem Iacob, quam diléxit.

content.latin: 46:6 Ascéndit Deus in iúbilo: * et Dóminus in voce tubæ.
content.english: 46:6 God is ascended with jubilee, * and the Lord with the sound of trumpet.

segments.t: Ascéndit Deus in iúbilo: * et Dóminus in voce tubæ.

content.latin: 46:7 Psállite Deo nostro, psállite: * psállite Regi nostro, psállite.
content.english: 46:7 Sing praises to our God, sing ye: * sing praises to our king, sing ye.

segments.t: Psállite Deo nostro, psállite: * psállite Regi nostro, psállite.

content.latin: 46:8 Quóniam Rex omnis terræ Deus: * psállite sapiénter.
content.english: 46:8 For God is the king of all the earth: * sing ye wisely.

segments.t: Quóniam Rex omnis terræ Deus: * psállite sapiénter.

content.latin: 46:9 Regnábit Deus super gentes: * Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam.
content.english: 46:9 God shall reign over the nations: * God sitteth on his holy throne.

segments.t: Regnábit Deus super gentes: * Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam.

content.latin: 46:10 Príncipes populórum congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham: * quóniam dii fortes terræ veheménter eleváti sunt.
content.english: 46:10 The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham: * for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted.

segments.t: Príncipes populórum congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham: * quóniam dii fortes terræ veheménter eleváti sunt.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Dignum sibi Dóminus computávit Mártyrem, quem vocávit Apóstolum, dum esset in mari, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. Whom the Lord called to be His Apostle, when he was by the sea, him also He counted worthy to be His martyr. Alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Dignum sibi Dóminus computávit Mártyrem, quem vocávit Apóstolum, dum esset in mari, allelúia.

content.latin: Ant. Diléxit Andréam * Dóminus in odórem suavitátis.
content.english: Ant. Andrew was to the Lord as a sweet savour, * which He loved exceedingly.

segments.t: Ant.
Diléxit Andréam * Dóminus in odórem suavitátis.

content.latin: Psalmus 60 [5]
content.english: Psalm 60 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 60

content.latin: 60:2 Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.
content.english: 60:2 Hear, O God, my supplication: * be attentive to my prayer.

segments.t: Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.

content.latin: 60:3 A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
content.english: 60:3 To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth: * when my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock.

segments.t: A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.

content.latin: 60:4 Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.
content.english: 60:4 Thou hast conducted me; for thou hast been my hope: * a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.

segments.t: Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.

content.latin: 60:5 Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.
content.english: 60:5 In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever: * I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings.

segments.t: Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.

content.latin: 60:6 Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.
content.english: 60:6 For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer: * thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.

content.latin: 60:7 Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos eius usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.
content.english: 60:7 Thou wilt add days to the days of the king: * his years even to generation and generation.

segments.t: Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos eius usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.

content.latin: 60:8 Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem eius quis requíret?
content.english: 60:8 He abideth for ever in the sight of God: * his mercy and truth who shall search?

segments.t: Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem eius quis requíret?

content.latin: 60:9 Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.
content.english: 60:9 So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever: * that I may pay my vows from day to day.

segments.t: Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.

content.english: Ant. The blessed Andrew hung alive upon the cross for two days * for Christ's Name's sake, and, all the while, he taught the people.

content.latin: Psalmus 63 [6]
content.english: Psalm 63 [6]

segments.t: Psalmus 63

content.latin: 63:2 Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam cum déprecor: * a timóre inimíci éripe ánimam meam.
content.english: 63:2 Hear, O God, my prayer, when I make supplication to thee: * deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.

segments.t: Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam cum déprecor: * a timóre inimíci éripe ánimam meam.

content.latin: 63:3 Protexísti me a convéntu malignántium: * a multitúdine operántium iniquitátem.
content.english: 63:3 Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant; * from the multitude of the workers of iniquity.

segments.t: Protexísti me a convéntu malignántium: * a multitúdine operántium iniquitátem.

content.latin: 63:4 Quia exacuérunt ut gládium linguas suas: * intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
content.english: 63:4 For they have whetted their tongues like a sword; * they have bent their bow a bitter thing, to shoot in secret the undefiled.

segments.t: Quia exacuérunt ut gládium linguas suas: * intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.

content.latin: 63:6 Súbito sagittábunt eum, et non timébunt: * firmavérunt sibi sermónem nequam.
content.english: 63:6 They will shoot at him on a sudden, and will not fear: * they are resolute in wickedness.

segments.t: Súbito sagittábunt eum, et non timébunt: * firmavérunt sibi sermónem nequam.

content.latin: 63:6 Narravérunt ut abscónderent láqueos: * dixérunt: Quis vidébit eos?
content.english: 63:6 They have talked of hiding snares; * they have said: Who shall see them?

segments.t: Narravérunt ut abscónderent láqueos: * dixérunt: Quis vidébit eos?

content.latin: 63:7 Scrutáti sunt iniquitátes: * defecérunt scrutántes scrutínio.
content.english: 63:7 They have searched after iniquities: * they have failed in their search.

segments.t: Scrutáti sunt iniquitátes: * defecérunt scrutántes scrutínio.

content.latin: 63:7 Accédet homo ad cor altum: * et exaltábitur Deus.
content.english: 63:7 Man shall come to a deep heart: * and God shall be exalted.

segments.t: Accédet homo ad cor altum: * et exaltábitur Deus.

content.latin: 63:8 Sagíttæ parvulórum factæ sunt plagæ eórum: * et infirmátæ sunt contra eos linguæ eórum.
content.english: 63:8 The arrows of children are their wounds: * and their tongues against them are made weak.

segments.t: Sagíttæ parvulórum factæ sunt plagæ eórum: * et infirmátæ sunt contra eos linguæ eórum.

content.latin: 63:9 Conturbáti sunt omnes qui vidébant eos: * et tímuit omnis homo.
content.english: 63:9 All that saw them were troubled; * and every man was afraid.

segments.t: Conturbáti sunt omnes qui vidébant eos: * et tímuit omnis homo.

content.latin: 63:10 Et annuntiavérunt ópera Dei, * et facta eius intellexérunt.
content.english: 63:10 And they declared the works of God: * and understood his doings.

segments.t: Et annuntiavérunt ópera Dei, * et facta eius intellexérunt.

content.latin: 63:11 Lætábitur iustus in Dómino, et sperábit in eo, * et laudabúntur omnes recti corde.
content.english: 63:11 The just shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in him: * and all the upright in heart shall be praised.

segments.t: Lætábitur iustus in Dómino, et sperábit in eo, * et laudabúntur omnes recti corde.

content.english: ℣. Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

content.latin: ℟. Mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.
content.english: ℟. They shall remember thy name, O Lord.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Ipsíus píetas et misericórdia nos ádiuvet, qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. May His loving-kindness and mercy help us, Who liveth and reigneth with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Ipsíus píetas et misericórdia nos ádiuvet, qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.english: Benediction. May God the Father Omnipotent, be to us merciful and clement.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Andréas Apóstolus, Bethsáidæ natus, qui est Galilǽæ vicus, frater Petri, discípulus Ioánnis Baptistæ, cum eum de Christo dicéntem audísset: Ecce Agnus Dei; secútus Iesum, fratrem quoque suum ad eúndem perdúxit. Cum póstea una cum fratre piscarétur in mari Galilǽæ, ambo a prætereúnte Christo Dómino ante álios Apóstolos vocáti illis verbis: Veníte post me, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum; nullam interponéntes moram, et relíctis rétibus, secúti sunt eum. Post cuius passiónem et resurrectiónem, Andréas, cum in Scýthiam Európæ, quæ ei província ad Christi fidem disseminándam obtígerat, venísset, deínde Epírum ac Thráciam peragrásset; doctrína et miráculis innumerábiles hómines ad Christum convértit. Post, Patras Acháiæ proféctus, et in ea urbe plúrimis ad veritátem evangélicam perdúctis, Ægéam procónsulem, prædicatióni evangélicæ resisténtem, libérrime increpávit, quod, qui iudex hóminum habéri vellet, Christum Deum ómnium iúdicem, a dæmónibus elúsus, non agnósceret.
content.english: The Apostle Andrew was born at Bethsaida, a town of Galilee, and was the brother of Peter. He was a disciple of John the Baptist, and heard him say of Christ, Behold the Lamb of God, John i. 35-37, 40, whereupon he immediately followed Jesus, bringing his brother also with him. Some while after, they were both fishing in the Sea of Galilee, and the Lord Christ, going by, called them both, before any other of the Apostles, in the words, Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men. They made no delay, but left their nets, and followed Him. ~Matth. iv. 18-20. After the death and Resurrection of Christ, Andrew was allotted Scythia as the province of his preaching, and, after labouring there, he went through Epirus and Thrace, where he turned vast multitudes to Christ by his teaching and miracles. Finally he went to Patras in Achaia, and there also he brought many to the knowledge of Gospel truth. Aegeas the Pro-consul resisted the preaching of the Gospel, and the Apostle freely rebuked him, bidding him know that while he held himself a judge of his fellow men, he was himself hindered by devils from knowing Christ our God, the Judge of all.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Homo Dei ducebátur ut crucifígerent eum: pópulus autem clamábat voce magna, dicens:
content.english: ℟. The man of God was led to be crucified, and the people cried with a loud voice, saying:

segments.t: Homo Dei ducebátur ut crucifígerent eum: pópulus autem clamábat voce magna, dicens:

content.latin: * Innocens eius sanguis sine causa damnátur.
content.english: * The innocent blood of this just person is condemned without a cause.

content.latin: ℣. Cumque dúcerent eum ut crucifigerétur, factus est concúrsus populórum clamántium et dicéntium.
content.english: ℣. And when they led him out to crucify him, all the people ran together and cried, saying

segments.t: Cumque dúcerent eum ut crucifigerétur, factus est concúrsus populórum clamántium et dicéntium.

content.latin: ℟. Innocens eius sanguis sine causa damnátur.
content.english: ℟. The innocent blood of this just person is condemned without a cause.

segments.t: Innocens eius sanguis sine causa damnátur.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Christus perpétuæ det nobis gáudia vitæ.
content.english: Benediction. May Christ to all His people give, for ever in His sight to live.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Christus perpétuæ det nobis gáudia vitæ.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Tum Ægéas irátus, Désine, inquit, Christum iactáre, cui simília verba nihil profuérunt, quóminus a Iudǽis crucifigerétur. Andréam vero de Christo nihilóminus líbere prædicántem quod pro salúte humáni géneris se crucifigéndum obtulísset, ímpia oratióne interpéllat, ac demum hortátur, ut sibi cónsulens, diis velit immoláre. Cui Andréas: Ego omnipoténti Deo, qui unus et verus est, ímmolo cotídie, non taurórum carnes, nec hircórum sánguinem, sed immaculátum Agnum in altári; cuius carnem posteáquam omnis pópulus credéntium manducáverit, Agnus, qui sacrificátus est, ínteger persevérat et vivus. Quam ob rem ira accénsus Ægéas, iubet eum in cárcerem detrúdi unde pópulus Andréam fácile liberásset, nisi ipse sedásset multitúdinem, veheméntius rogans, ne se ad optatíssimam martýrii corónam properántem impedírent.
content.english: Then Egeas, being angry, answered him, Boast no more of this thy Christ. He spake words even such as thine, but they availed Him not, and He was crucified by the Jews. Whereto Andrew boldly answered that Christ had given Himself up to die for man's salvation; but the Pro-consul blasphemously interrupted him, and bade him look to himself, and sacrifice to the gods. Then said Andrew, We have an altar, whereon day by day I offer up to God, the Almighty, the One, and the True, not the flesh of bulls nor the blood of goats, but a Lamb without spot and when all they that believe have eaten of the Flesh Thereof, the Lamb That was slain abideth whole and liveth. Then Aegeas being filled with wrath, bound the Apostle in prison. Now, the people would have delivered him, but he himself calmed the multitude, and earnestly besought them not to take away from him the crown of martyrdom, for which he longed and which was now drawing near.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. O bona crux, quæ decórem et pulchritúdinem de membris Dómini suscepísti; áccipe me ab homínibus, et redde me magístro meo:
content.english: ℟. O precious cross, which the Members of my Lord have made so fair and goodly, welcome me from among men, and join me again to my Master,

segments.t: O bona crux, quæ decórem et pulchritúdinem de membris Dómini suscepísti; áccipe me ab homínibus, et redde me magístro meo:

content.latin: * Ut per te me recípiat, qui per te me redémit.
content.english: * That, as by thee He redeemed me, so by thee also He may take me unto Himself.

content.latin: ℣. Beátus Andréas expánsis mánibus ad cælum orábat, dicens: Salva me, bona crux.
content.english: ℣. The blessed Andrew stretched forth his hands to heaven and prayed, saying: Precious cross, be my salvation,

segments.t: Beátus Andréas expánsis mánibus ad cælum orábat, dicens: Salva me, bona crux.

content.latin: ℟. Ut per te me recípiat, qui per te me redémit.
content.english: ℟. That, as by thee He redeemed me, so by thee also He may take me unto Himself.

segments.t: Ut per te me recípiat, qui per te me redémit.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ignem sui amóris accéndat Deus in córdibus nostris.
content.english: Benediction. May the Spirit's fire Divine in our hearts enkindled shine.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Ignem sui amóris accéndat Deus in córdibus nostris.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Igitur paulo post in tribúnal prodúctum, cum Ægéas crucis extolléntem mystéria sibíque suam impietátem exprobrántem diútius ferre non posset, in crucem tolli, et Christi mortem imitári iussit. Addúctus Andréas ad locum martýrii, cum crucem vidísset, longe exclamáre cœpit: O bona crux, quæ decórem ex membris Dómini suscepísti, diu desideráta, sollícite amáta, sine intermissióne quæsíta, et aliquándo cupiénti ánimo præparáta: áccipe me ab homínibus, et redde me magístro meo; ut per te me recípiat, qui per te me redémit. Itaque cruci affíxus est: in qua bíduum vivus pendens, et Christi fidem prædicáre nunquam intermíttens, ad eum migrávit, cuius mortis similitúdinem concupíerat. Quæ ómnia presbýteri et diáconi Acháiæ, qui eius passiónem scripsérunt, se ita ut commemoráta sunt, audísse et vidísse testántur. Eius ossa primum Constantíno imperatóre Constantinópolim, deínde Amálphim transláta sunt. Caput, Pio secúndo Pontífice, Romam allátum, in basílica sancti Petri collocátum est.
content.english: Come a short while after, he was brought before the judgment-seat, where he extolled the mystery of the cross, and rebuked Aegeas for his ungodliness. Then Aegeas could bear with him no longer, but commanded him to be crucified, in imitation of Christ. Andrew, then, was led to the place of martyrdom, and, as soon as he came in sight of the cross, he cried out, O precious cross, which the Members of my Lord have made so goodly, how long have I desired thee! how warmly have I loved thee! how constantly have I sought thee! And, now that thou art come to me, how is my soul drawn to thee! Welcome me from among men, and join me again to my Master, that as by thee He redeemed me, so by thee also He may take me unto Himself. So he was fastened to the cross, whereon he hung living for two days, during which time he ceased not to preach the faith of Christ, and, finally, passed into the Presence of Him the likeness of Whose death he had loved so well. All the above particulars of his last sufferings were written by the Priests and Deacons of Achaia, who bear witness to them of their own knowledge. Under the Emperor Constantine the bones of the Apostle were first taken to Constantinople, whence they were afterwards brought to Amalfi. In the Pontificate of Pope Pius II his head was carried to Rome, where it is kept in the Basilica of St. Peter.

content.latin: Audístis, fratres caríssimi, quia ad uníus iussiónis vocem Petrus et Andréas relíctis rétibus secúti sunt Redemptórem. Nulla vero hunc fácere adhuc mirácula víderant, nihil ab eo de prǽmio ætérnæ retributiónis audíerant: et tamen ad unum Dómini præcéptum hoc quod possidére videbántur, oblíti sunt. Quanta nos eius mirácula vidémus, quot flagéllis afflígimur, quantis minárum asperitátibus deterrémur, et tamen vocántem sequi contémnimus.
content.english: Dearly beloved brethren, ye hear how that Peter and Andrew, having once heard the Lord call them, left their nets, and followed their Saviour. As yet they had seen none of His miracles, as yet they had received no promise of their exceeding and eternal reward; nevertheless, at one word of the Lord they forgot all those things which they seemed to have. We have seen many of His miracles; we have received many of His gracious chastenings; many times hath He warned us of the wrath to come and yet Christ calleth and we do not follow.

content.latin: ℟. Orávit sanctus Andréas, dum respíceret in cælum, et voce magna clamávit et dixit: Tu es Deus meus, quem vidi: ne me patiáris ab ímpio iúdice depóni:
content.english: ℟. The holy Andrew lifted up his eyes to heaven, and prayed, and cried with a loud voice, and said: Thou art my God, Whom I have seen; suffer not the unjust judge to take me down from the cross

segments.t: Orávit sanctus Andréas, dum respíceret in cælum, et voce magna clamávit et dixit: Tu es Deus meus, quem vidi: ne me patiáris ab ímpio iúdice depóni:

content.latin: * Quia virtútem sanctæ crucis agnóvi.

segments.t: Tu es magíster meus Christus, quem diléxi, quem cognóvi, quem conféssus sum: tantúmmodo in ista voce exáudi me.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: In cælo iam sedet, qui de conversióne nos ádmonet; iam iugo fídei colla géntium súbdidit, iam mundi glóriam stravit, iam ruínis eius crebrescéntibus, distrícti sui iudícii diem propinquántem denúntiat: et tamen supérba mens nostra adhuc non vult hoc sponte desérere, quod cotídie perdit invíta. Quid ergo, fratres caríssimi, quid in eius iudício dictúri sumus, qui ab amóre præséntis sǽculi nec præcéptis fléctimur, nec verbéribus emendámur?
content.english: He who calleth us to be converted is now enthroned in heaven; He hath broken the necks of the Gentiles to the yoke of the faith, He hath laid low the glory of the world, and the wrecks thereof, falling ever more and more to decay, do preach unto us that the coming of that day when He is to be revealed as our Judge is drawing nigh and yet, so stubborn is our mind, that we will not yet freely abandon that which, will we, nill we, we lose day by day. Dearly beloved brethren, what shall we answer at His judgment-seat, we whom no lessons can persuade, and no stripes can break of the love of this present world?

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.english: ℟. When Andrew saw the cross he cried, saying: How wonderful art thou, O cross! O cross, how loveable art thou! O cross, thy bright beams enlighten the darkness of the whole world!

segments.t: Videns crucem Andréas exclamávit, dicens: O crux admirábilis, o crux desiderábilis, o crux quæ per totum mundum rútilas:

content.english: Benediction. May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Sed fortásse áliquis tácitis sibi cogitatiónibus dicat: Ad vocem Domínicam utérque iste piscátor quid, aut quantum dimísit, qui pene nihil hábuit? Sed hac in re, fratres caríssimi, afféctum debémus pótius pensáre quam censum. Multum relíquit, qui sibi nihil retínuit: multum relíquit, qui quantúmlibet parum, totum deséruit. Certe nos et hábita cum amóre possidémus, et ea, quæ mínime habémus, ex desidério quǽrimus. Multum ergo Petrus et Andréas dimísit, quando utérque étiam desidéria habéndi derelíquit.
content.english: Perhaps one perchance will ask in his heart, what Peter or Andrew had to lose by obeying the call of the Lord? Dearly beloved brethren, we must consider here rather the intention than the loss incurred by this obedience. He that keepeth nothing for himself, giveth up much; he that sacrificeth his all, sacrificed what is to him a great deal. Beyond doubt, we cling to whatever we have, and what we have least, that we desire most. Peter and Andrew therefore gave up much when they gave up even the desire of possessing anything.

content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Te Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
content.english: We praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.

content.latin: Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
content.english: All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.

content.latin: Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
content.english: To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.

content.latin: Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
content.english: To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.

content.english: bow head Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;

segments.t: Fit reverentia
Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.

content.latin: Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.

content.latin: Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
content.english: The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
content.english: The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
content.english: The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.

content.latin: Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
content.english: The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;

content.latin: Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
content.english: The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.

content.latin: Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
content.english: Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;

content.latin: Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
content.english: Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.

content.latin: Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
content.english: Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.

content.latin: Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
content.english: Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
content.english: During the following verse all make a profound bow: When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.

segments.t: Fit reverentia
Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.

content.latin: Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
content.english: When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.

content.latin: Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
content.english: Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.

content.latin: Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
content.english: We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.

content.latin: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
content.english: Kneel for the following verse We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.

segments.t: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus
Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.

content.latin: Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
content.english: Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.

content.latin: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
content.english: O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.

content.latin: Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.

content.latin: Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
content.english: Day by day * we magnify thee;

content.latin: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow. And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.

segments.t: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem
Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
content.english: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.

content.latin: Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.

content.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
content.english: O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

segments.t: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Maiestátem tuam, Dómine, supplíciter exorámus: ut, sicut Ecclésiæ tuæ beátus Andréas Apóstolus éxstitit prædicátor et rector; ita apud te sit pro nobis perpétuus intercéssor.
content.english: O Lord, we humbly beseech thy Majesty, that even as Thou didst give thy blessed Apostle Andrew to thy Church to be a teacher and a ruler on earth, so, now that he is with thee, he may continually make intercession for us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
